pins.configOverlay: floe-config/floe_android_mbedtls_config.h — full copy of include/mbedtls/mbedtls_config.h with exactly ONE documented hunk (FLOE-ANDROID-PATCH 20261024-1 disables MBEDTLS_SSL_PROTO_TLS1_3; libgit2 1.9.2 never calls psa_crypto_init(), so the TLS ceiling is TLS 1.2 with libgit2's ECDHE/AEAD suite list; GitHub requires TLS 1.2+, so no promised connectivity is lost). Injected via -DMBEDTLS_CONFIG_FILE; it is a data header, not a C source edit.

whyNotOtherBackends: Upstream libgit2 Package.swift selects Apple vs non-Apple settings with host-evaluated #if os(macOS); an android28 cross build from a macOS host compiles the SecureTransport/CommonCrypto branch against the Android target and fails. The vendored overlay manifests replace host-evaluation with per-platform .when(platforms:) conditions only.
The upstream non-Apple branch targets OpenSSL dlopen at runtime (GIT_HTTPS_OPENSSL_DYNAMIC); Android exposes no public system libssl/libcrypto, so dynamic OpenSSL cannot deliver HTTPS on Android.

OpenSSL 3.x static requires its perl-driven Configure, breaking the one-command SwiftPM native build and adding an unverifiable external artifact boundary; mbedTLS compiles as plain C inside the same graph.
libgit2 1.9.2's mbedTLS stream backend predates the 3.x psa-only TLS 1.3 stack; the documented config hunk keeps TLS 1.2 fully functional instead of patching upstream C.
vendored binary blobs, floating refs, system-provided Android TLS and guest git are all explicitly forbidden or substituted-away routes for this lane (task + Main D2).
